name: The orb roster
summary: Ten selectable orbs ship, listed in LAB_ORBS; three ids do not match their on-screen names (warp=SLOW-MO, spot=MAGNET, hyper=HYPERNOVA).
detail: LAB_ORBS is the roster of record: tools/check.mjs compares its n: names against MECHANICS.md, and smoke.mjs derives its lab sweep from it. An orb added to spawnPow but not to LAB_ORBS is invisible to both. The id drift is save compatibility, not sloppiness -- spot/spotPlaced/spotGlow/stagelight survive the Spotlight-to-Magnet redesign so existing G.upg and preference keys keep working.

name: SHIELD
summary: Green banked orb: one hit each, spent automatically for 0.9s of invulnerability; cap is 3/4/5 by difficulty clock and every run starts with two.
detail: Home level 1, first of the POW_INTRO trio (shield -> slow-mo -> nova), placed once per RUN on G.introN. A hit spends one, sets G.invuln=G.t+0.9 and knocks you off the orbit but deliberately does NOT clear lapAcc or lapStreak. Picking one up at a full bank pays a flat +50 instead of banking. Drawn from power-shield.webp when the texture is present, otherwise a mint faceted crystal with a cross-in-shield glyph.

name: Overcharge (full shield bank)
summary: While the shield bank is full, embers pay double and a tight tap pays a flat +8; an overflow shield pays +50, and the orbit payout is untouched.
detail: Not an orb: a state the shield orb opens. G.shields>=shieldMax() is one arm of the standing-state doubling branch alongside overdrive and hypernova, and one arm of the flat +8 tight-tap branch. The announcement 'Shields full: stars now score double' waits for G.seen.single so the red lesson lands first; cueState(true) opens the shimmer either way. shieldMax() stepping 3->4->5 at dl 160/320 silently ends a full bank, which is why BANK DEEPER exists.

name: SLOW-MO (id `warp`)
summary: Violet orb: six seconds at 55% speed, nine with SLOW WORLD; the dilation rides G.tsCur so the whole visible world slows, not just the simulation.
detail: Home level 1, second of the POW_INTRO trio. The pickup sets G.slow and G.slowD and says 'Slow-mo: movement slows for Ns'. The target timescale tsT is 0.55 while G.slow>0 (a black hole outranks it at BH_TS 0.60, or 0.372 during the opening warp) and G.tsCur eases toward it asymmetrically -- 3.2/s going down, 8/s coming back. Sprite key is power-slow, not power-warp.

name: NOVA
summary: White orb: one expanding front converts the shards present at pickup into reachable stars on the player's own ring, with 0.95s of grace covering the sweep.
detail: Home level 1, third of the POW_INTRO trio, and the only pickup branch that names no type -- it is the final else of the chain, which is why a static 'one branch per orb id' scan cannot find it. novaBlast snapshots G.spikes into targets, so threats spawning after the blast are never erased; the front's own expiry converts nothing. Speed is max(560*u, (2R+60u)/0.62) so a wide viewport still clears the ring system inside the grace.

name: novaConvert -- the shared red-to-star path
summary: One function turns an armed shard into collectable embers on the player's ring, and five separate rewards route through it: nova, hypernova, mirror, scorch and slipstream.
detail: The ember lands on the ring the PLAYER is on (or an explicit toRing, which only slipstream passes) at the shard's angle, stepping 0.36 rad in the travel direction up to 8 times until it has 0.30 rad of clearance -- so a converted wall reads as a necklace, never a pile. RICH NOVA emits two and both walk that same spacing search. Each conversion also takes the next sixteenth slot and the next pentatonic degree, so a cascade plays a strict ascending run; a gap of more than 0.8s restarts the run from the bottom.

name: HYPERNOVA (id `hyper`)
summary: Magenta orb, level 2's guarantee: sixteen beats (9.231s) of invincibility at up to +90% speed, converting every red you plow through into a paying ember.
detail: G.hyperD = SPB * (LONGER STAR ? 24 : 16). Speed is speedAt()*(1+0.9*hv) where hv = min(1, (hyperD-hyper)/0.35, hyper/1.4) -- a 0.35s ease in, a 1.4s ease out, so the star never dumps you at double speed into an armed lane; expiry then grants G.t+1.2 of grace. Armed red met while it burns is routed to novaConvert ahead of the shield branch. Stars pay double while it burns and a tight tap pays a flat +8; the orbit payout, as everywhere, is untouched. Named HYPERNOVA in every channel after shipping as 'the pink star' in one.

name: STARRUN -- the hypernova's tune
summary: Sixteen sixteenths of pentatonic degrees 4-10 that climb and wrap, restated every bar over an eighth-note bass, added as an overlay rather than a third section.
detail: STARRUN is [4,5,6,7, 5,6,7,8, 6,7,8,9, 7,8,9,10] -- four ascending four-note cells each starting a degree higher, so the line spirals and never resolves. It is an overlay because a section change can only land at a four-bar seam, which can be most of a loop away against a star that lasts four bars; applySect is the only writer of CH/ARP and a mid-bar harmony swap would break the rule the payoff, rise, black hole and star dive exceptions exist to protect. Written as degrees so it transposes with the level key, and it sits above the band's degree-4 arp ceiling. powerColour returns immediately while G.hyper>0, so the mirror and scorch voices yield to it; a black hole outranks it.

name: The hypernova's comet tail
summary: A hypernova widens the ribbon 1.85x, crossfades its three passes to the orb's magenta and gold, doubles the particle ceiling and sheds sparks without a groove chain.
detail: Everything rides G.hyperGlow rather than G.hyper, so it arrives and leaves with the corona instead of snapping with the timer; at hyperGlow 0 the arithmetic reduces to the ordinary ribbon. Half-width gains (1+0.85*hyperGlow), trailCap climbs 62 -> 110 samples, the wake ceiling goes 80 -> 160 particles and the spawn interval is divided by up to 3.2. DRIFT WORTH KNOWING: MECHANICS.md and powerups.md both say the star draws 'five passes instead of three'. As of commit 01a3a25 the pass table holds three entries (two when ghosted) and the star is expressed as an hmix colour crossfade on those three, not as extra passes.

name: The HYPERNOVA x2 chip does not exist
summary: MECHANICS.md and powerups.md both describe a standing 'HYPERNOVA x2' HUD chip; the code draws a named seconds countdown and the string appears nowhere in runtime.js.
detail: drawPowerStatus builds rows of [label, remaining, duration, colour] -- Hypernova, Magnet, Mirror, Scorch, Slipstream, Slow-mo, Star trail -- each drawn as a name, ceil(seconds)+'s' and a progress bar. No multiplier chip exists for any orb. The only NOUN x N examples in the file are in the house-style comment that defines the idiom. SPOTLIGHT x2 is the same case one orb along.

name: MAGNET (id `spot`)
summary: Level 3's guarantee: for 10 seconds stars within 110 scale units on the current or an adjacent ring curve into the moving comet over a 0.38s flight.
detail: Captures stars only -- never shards -- gated on Math.abs(s.ring-effRing())<=1 and a distance test against MAGNET_RANGE. Each capture builds a quadratic Bezier whose control point is bent min(22, d*0.28) perpendicular to the line of flight and extends the star's own life so it survives the trip. starVisualPos is authoritative for contact, crystal, bloom and route links. updateMagnetStar returns immediately while bhActive(), so both attraction and captured-star lifetimes freeze inside a black hole. There is no star or tap multiplier and no temporary instrument mode.

name: THE MIRROR
summary: Level 4's guarantee: a second comet at G.angle+PI on your own ring for sixteen beats that gathers stars and shatters armed red, pays, but never advances the combo.
detail: Its angle is DERIVED every frame, never integrated -- a chaser that accumulates its own position drifts and needs a controller, and the magnetar died twice proving a first-order chase never arrives. Contact uses the same swept arc the player's pickup check uses and stays on the old ring through the first half of a hop. It skips st.trail and st.mag stars: the offered route and a star already flying to the player belong to the player. It pays max(1, G.combo) and leaves the chain where it found it. It cannot be hurt and it does not protect you.

name: SCORCH
summary: Level 5's guarantee: for 8 seconds the arc of your own ring you have travelled stays lit and destroys any red standing in or arming into it.
detail: A full lap makes a full lap safe; sitting still makes almost nothing safe -- that asymmetry is the design, and it is the saucer's camping problem answered from the reward side. Stored as 72 sectors per ring in a Float32Array (four rings allocated once per run) because sectors cannot overlap or leak. Painted from G.prevAngle to the current angle in ceil(sweep/step) samples, so nothing is skipped at 4.2 rad/s. Sector lifetime is max(BURN_LIFE, TAU/max(0.3,G.speed)+0.2) in GAMEPLAY seconds, so slow motion preserves the wake. Drawn under the shards. Warm orange, deliberately not warm red.

name: SLIPSTREAM (id `slip`)
summary: Level 2's second guarantee: for 12 seconds each successful hop converts non-saucer shards within 0.48 rad of the landing angle into stars on that destination ring.
detail: It fires inside hop() AFTER the ring index is committed, so only a successful player hop counts: an invalid swipe returns before that point and black-hole gravity moves G.ringI directly in bhTick without calling hop(). The clear happens on every valid hop, but the 0.4s landing grace is metered by G.slipAt at most once per 0.8s, so chained swipes cannot become continuous immunity. Saucers are exempt from the clear. It is the only one of novaConvert's five call sites that passes an explicit destination ring.

name: STAR TRAIL (id `trail`)
summary: Level 3's second guarantee: nine marked gold stars laid 0.62 rad apart ahead in the current direction, alternating two rings, each paying the combo plus four bonus points.
detail: layStarTrail filters out every existing trail star first, so a later pickup replaces the route rather than stacking. Stars sit at G.angle + dir*(0.62 + i*0.62); odd indices go to the adjacent ring (inward if the comet is on the innermost, outward otherwise). Each collects through the ordinary swept-contact path, advances the combo, and adds STAR_ROUTE_BONUS on top. Red stays on the board, so following the route is an active choice, and collecting in order is an invitation rather than a rule. The mirror deliberately leaves route stars for the player.

name: BLACK HOLE
summary: The one optional, dangerous orb: a 17-second mode on a temporary fourth ring, guaranteed to be OFFERED once on level 4 and otherwise a 5% roll from level 3.
detail: Phases: 0 off, 1 opening (BH_WARP 0.85s), 2 challenge, 3 closing. Ring zero is OUTERMOST throughout. The escape signal opens at BH_ESCAPE and the deadline is BH_DUR. Motion runs at BH_TS after the warp; density climbs from 1.25 to 2 across the pre-escape window; gravity pulls one ring inward every BH_PULL seconds until escape opens. Placement arms bhCool = t+20 (the decline price); actually taking it arms t+55 on the event. Its MEET lesson is the only orb lesson that is NOT soft, because taking it starts a mode rather than granting a gift.

name: The black hole's cash-out
summary: Escaping pays round((80 + 600*charge + 20*stars) / 1.5^min(3,shieldsSpent)); missing the deadline costs the bank and one shield, or ends an unshielded run.
detail: charge accrues at dt/8 only while settled on the innermost ring before escape opens, so eight seconds of inner-ring travel fills it; entry alone awards nothing. BH.score counts stars collected during phase 2. shieldsSpent is measured as G.blocks minus the count at entry, so the divisor prices being saved during the mode. Inner-ring stars pay double during phase 2 -- and that bonus was on the WRONG ring once, because index 0 is the outermost orbit.

name: Starfall
summary: Not a spawned orb: the payout for three star-fed orbits (two with EARLY STARFALL), released automatically on the next musical quarter, never asking for a different tap.
detail: build(amount,src) is the only charge entry point and discards everything that is not src==='orbit' with amount>=0.04, so time, embers, hops, taps and near-miss grazes contribute nothing. On the qualifying orbit armDrop schedules the release on the grid when WebAudio is live; with no audio startStarfall fires immediately. The release opens with novaBlast from the arena centre, clearing the board, and holds G.invuln at t+left+0.6 for the whole window. DROP_STEP and DROP_STEP_MAX are both 0 -- the escalating-cost curve the long comment above them describes is retired.

name: Starfall's three waves and its doubling
summary: Three waves of five stars arrive at 0, 3.077 and 6.154 seconds of the 9.231-second window, and each collected star adds its combo value a second time.
detail: starfallWave pushes five stars per wave (capped at 30 stars on the board) at G.angle + dir*(0.55 + j*0.42); every third one (j%3===2) goes to the adjacent ring -- inward if the comet is on the innermost, outward otherwise. Each lives 5 seconds and carries starfall:true. Outside reduced-motion each also carries a `flight` arc thrown in from the level's planet, staggered delay j*0.065 over a duration 0.68+j*0.045, and it is uncollectable until its delay elapses. tickStarfall schedules the next wave every PAYLEN/3. The doubling is an if/else against the standing-state doubling, so hypernova/overdrive/full-bank never stack with it; G.secMult is always 1 today, so that multiply is a no-op left from the retired perfect-landing rule.

name: spawnPow's branch ladder
summary: A single if/else chain decides every placement: lab, intro trio, shield pity, black hole, then the six guarantees, then the weighted POWPOOL roll.
detail: Order is the design: an earlier branch always wins. The two black-hole branches sit directly below the intro trio and above every guarantee, deliberately -- the guarantee flags are patient and survive a delayed placement, while an unrolled per-placement die is simply gone. Note that the mirror (level 4) is tested before Magnet (level 3), so a run that reaches level 4 with spotPlaced still false is handed the mirror first. The pity shield outranks every optional offer, including the black hole.

name: POWPOOL -- the fallback weights
summary: The nine-row [id, weight, minLevel] table behind the guarantees; weights sum to 1.190 and are renormalised over the rows the current level unlocks.
detail: The first seven rows sum to exactly 1.000 -- the roster before SLIPSTREAM and STAR TRAIL, which were appended at 0.095 each rather than taken out of the existing space. ptot is recomputed over eligible rows every call, so what a player sees is weight/ptot: at level 1 that is 47.9/29.4/22.7 for shield/warp/nova, and at level 5-6 it is 25.4/15.5/12.0/11.3/6.4/6.7/6.7/8.0/8.0 across all nine. blackhole is NOT in the table; it arrives only from its own two branches. Nothing outside runtime.js reads POWPOOL.

name: The once-per-RUN guarantee flags
summary: hyperPlaced, spotPlaced, mirrorPlaced, scorchPlaced, slipPlaced and trailPlaced survive level boundaries and start pre-spent for every home level a run opens past.
detail: startGame() re-arms them only when the run is not carrying a score forward, and even then sets each to (G.level > homeLevel). So a 1->6 climb meets each orb exactly once on its home level, and a REDSHIFT start is not owed four marquee placements in its first minute. Re-arming at every boundary was a real shipped bug: one measured climb guaranteed HYPERNOVA on L2, L3, L4, L5 and L6 and buried level 5's own two introductions. bhPlaced is different -- it is cleared by every startGame, and bhRun is the flag that survives.

name: The shield-pity rule
summary: Three placements without a shield forces the next one to be a shield, and the branch sits above the black hole so an optional event can never postpone survival.
detail: G.sinceShield counts PLACEMENTS, not pickups -- otherwise a run spent dodging would serve nothing but shields forever. It resets to 0 on a shield and increments on everything else. A pity shield placed while the intro trio still owes one also advances G.introN, because the thing the slot exists to show has just been shown. No harness anywhere reads sinceShield.

name: Orb spawn cadence and lifetime
summary: One orb on the board at a time, never during the finale, Starfall or a black hole; it lives 7 seconds and the next arms at max(6, rand(10,15) - dl*0.02).
detail: A run opens with powT = 4 which, with the dl()>=6 gate, puts the first shield on the board around ten seconds in. A failed placement retries in 0.5s. In the lab the refill is rand(2.2, 3.6) instead, bought entirely on the refill so the one-orb-at-a-time gate is preserved -- two on the board at once is not a thing the real game ever does, and a rig that shows an arrangement the game cannot produce is testing the wrong object.

name: Where an orb may be placed
summary: Up to 24 tries at a random angle and ring, each accepted only if farFromAll(a, ring, 0.6, sep(ring,3.2), sep(ring,3.0)) clears it of the player, stars and shards.
detail: Rewards keep the OLD symmetric player clearance rather than the heading-aware bubble the hazard pass uses: letting stars and orbs fill in behind a stationary player would hand the camper a reason to stay, which is the behaviour the asymmetric rule exists to price. If all 24 attempts fail, spawnPow returns false, no flag is spent and powT is set to 0.5 for a quick retry.

name: POW_LESSON and the guarantee that is of the INTRODUCTION
summary: An unseen musical orb that expires unlessoned clears its own placed flag, so the guarantee is of the lesson landing rather than of one spawn roll.
detail: POW_LESSON maps orb id -> guarantee flag for spot, hyper, mirror, scorch, slip, trail and blackhole. firstMeet is called at placement AND re-offered every frame the orb is still on the board, because the single call at placement can hit a busy moment and defer. Two writers spend a lesson, not one: firstMeet fires the sentence, and the pickup path separately treats TAKING a musical orb as having been taught it -- both are guarded against the lab, and the harness found the second.

name: The seven orb MEET lessons
summary: Six reward orbs carry soft:1 first-encounter sentences (no time dilation); the black hole's is deliberately hard, because taking it starts a mode rather than granting a gift.
detail: Shield, slow-mo and nova have no MEET row: they are taught by the level-1 card, the hint ladder and their own say() line at pickup. A hard lesson additionally refuses to fire while any timed reward is live (hyper, spot, slow, mirror, scorch, slip or a live route), because 2.8 frozen seconds is a third of the marquee item burned while the player cannot move. smoke.mjs only asserts the soft flag for spot, hyper and lapcost -- mirror, scorch, slip and trail could lose it silently.

values.spot: Magnet: nearby stars curve into you for 10 seconds
values.hyper: Hypernova: move faster, safe from red, for about 9s
values.mirror: Mirror: a second comet collects stars and clears red for about 9s
values.scorch: Scorch: your path clears red obstacles for 8s
values.slip: Slipstream: swipe rings to clear nearby red for 12s
values.trail: Star trail: collect nine bonus stars within 16s
values.blackhole: Black hole: ride the inner ring; at ESCAPE, swipe to the outer ring

name: POWERUP TESTING (the lab)
summary: A sandbox that places one chosen orb every ~3 seconds on a board pinned at dl 40, bypassing the intro trio, level floors, guarantees, shield pity and the black hole's rarity.
detail: LAB.on short-circuits spawnPow's first branch. LAB_DL is 40 -- exactly TIERS[3].at, the lowest clock value that gives the arena all three orbits, because the black hole opens a FOURTH on entry and a one-ring lab would demonstrate that against nothing. The ghost (red cannot touch you, on by default) is read at the single lethal-contact site ahead of the hypernova and shield branches, so nothing downstream fires. Nothing a lab session does reaches the device: no record, no run count, no lesson, no preference, and only one telemetry event. The LAB literal carries type:'blackhole', but enterPowerSel immediately overwrites it from LAB.sel, so the orb actually armed on a fresh visit is LAB_ORBS[5] -- the mirror.

name: Which orbs have sprite art
summary: Nine of the ten orbs map to a power-*.webp texture; `spot` (Magnet) is absent from artKey by design and always draws its procedural horseshoe crystal.
detail: artifactSprite bakes a sprite at the current scale from host.getTexture(artKey) when present and falls back to the faceted crystal plus artifactGlyph otherwise. docs/art/catalog.json marks power-spotlight.webp 'Retired Spotlight art; not the current Magnet. Do not map to runtime spot.' -- yet it is still in public/art/manifest.json and BootScene loads every manifest texture, so 25.7KB of retired art is fetched and decoded on every boot for a key nothing reads. drawPow routes everything except the black hole to artifactPower; the black hole keeps a hand-drawn fallback used only when its texture is absent.

name: The timed-reward HUD rows
summary: drawPowerStatus draws one row per live timed reward -- name, ceil(seconds)+'s' and a progress bar -- and returns immediately during a black hole or the intro.
detail: Rows are Hypernova, Magnet, Mirror, Scorch, Slipstream, Slow-mo and Star trail. Star trail's countdown is derived from any live s.trail star's remaining life rather than a separate timer. On a wide viewport the list sits in the right margin beside the arena; otherwise it stacks under the header in up to two columns. Magnet is drawn in COL.comet here while its arc flash is COL.warp and its pickup burst is #eaf1ff -- three different colours for one orb, and it shares the cyan with Slipstream on the same list.

name: Ordinary rewards suspend inside a black hole
summary: updateOrbMotion returns immediately while bhActive(), so mirror, scorch, slipstream, magnet attraction, route lifetimes and Starfall consume no time inside the mode.
detail: Remaining reward time resumes after the closing warp. The ember loop skips trail, mag and starfall stars entirely while bhActive() and ages them on rewardDt otherwise. updateMagnetStar returns early too, so a captured star freezes mid-flight rather than finishing into a comet the mode has moved. No orb spawns during the mode at all -- an orb in here is either a lifeline undoing the difficulty the mode exists to create, or a musical orb whose effect is on an arrangement that is halted.

name: What the harnesses assert about orbs
summary: Six orbs have their pickup effect asserted in smoke.mjs; shield, hypernova and the black hole have none, and nothing anywhere reads sinceShield, POWPOOL or overcharge.
detail: smoke.mjs calls pickup() for warp, slip, trail, mirror, scorch and spot only; nova is exercised through a direct novaBlast call and the black hole through startBlackHole. Its lab sweep plays every LAB_ORBS row for 45 seconds and requires at least two placements of that type and no other, which is the broadest placement guarantee in the suite and grows with the roster for free. fxcheck proves all eight non-shield orb kinds can own a visible scene event. curriculum requires a reachable lesson for the six musical orbs and the level-2/level-3 guarantee pairs.

name: The ledger-drift guard, and what it cannot see
summary: check.mjs fails the build if any TIERS name or LAB_ORBS name is absent from MECHANICS.md; it is a lowercase substring test, one-directional, and it never reads UPG.
detail: All ten LAB_ORBS names and all eleven UPG names appear in MECHANICS.md today, and every orb has a real row or section rather than an incidental mention -- so the rule is currently satisfied. What the guard cannot catch: a ledger row describing behaviour the code no longer has (the HYPERNOVA x2 chip), a row filed under the wrong heading (Magnet sits in the level-2 table while its own cell says level 3), a twelfth upgrade tile, or an orb added to spawnPow but never to LAB_ORBS. The names.length<8 floor exists because a regex that stops matching yields an empty list and an empty loop reports success.

name: SPOTLIGHT (replaced by MAGNET)
summary: Not removed but redesigned in place after the owner found its stage metaphor confusing; its ids (spot, spotPlaced, spotGlow, stagelight) all survive for save compatibility.
detail: The review that killed it found its active state changed ZERO arena pixels for its whole nine-to-fourteen seconds: the entire inventory was an audio mix move (instrument x1.5, pad to 0.8) plus a text chip that only drew on tall viewports, and its one universal effect -- stars paying double -- printed the UNDOUBLED number in its popup. Fixing that popup lie repaired the same bug for overdrive, hypernova and overcharge, all of which were adding 2x while printing 1x. Its art still ships and is still loaded; nothing reads it.

name: THE BASS BOMB (removed)
summary: Cut by the owner because its whole identity lived in the audio channel: with sound off it was a weaker nova over a never-drawn wedge, and LONG FUSE widened an invisible number.
detail: Its visual tell -- a subwoofer cone slamming on the beat -- rode G.beat, which only moves when the audio scheduler feeds it, so for a muted player the sprite sat motionless and the pickup was a cyan flash. What remained was the same novaConvert pipeline over a +/-60 degree wedge instead of the whole board, without invulnerability, at the same rotation odds. Two orbs occupying one job, one of them inferior and illegible, is one orb too many. Its 0.15 share was redistributed proportionally, which is the standing rule for a removal.

name: THE MAGNETAR (removed)
summary: Died twice proving a first-order chase never arrives on a circular board, which is why THE MIRROR derives its angle instead of integrating one.
detail: It is also why check.mjs forbids any second radius on an ember or an orb: the magnetar gave embers a free radius in s.pr so they could curve between rings, the bloom pass never read it, and sixteen glows sat detached from their embers by up to 89px on a 390px screen. The guard is inverted deliberately -- rather than police two radii staying in sync, it fails if a second radius is assigned at all. Its 0.11 share was redistributed proportionally.

name: ECHO and METEOR -- banned teaching keys
summary: check.mjs fails the build only when MEET or teachSoft references 'echo' or 'meteor'; the docs overstate this as a banned string, and both words appear elsewhere freely.
detail: The guard is a regex over (MEET= or teachSoft=) followed by the quoted id, so it catches teaching data outliving a cut orb and nothing else. ECHO was the runner-up name for THE MIRROR, which was called THE TWIN as a working name and renamed because TWIN SHARDS is a formation met at dl 18. METEOR is a second cut orb whose name survives nowhere else in the design record.

name: The upgrade draft
summary: Three of eleven tiles are offered at each of the five level-complete cards; there is no currency, the cost is the choice, and a taken tile never returns.
detail: levelComplete() calls rollOffer() when G.level+1 <= LEVEL_MAX and tapping a tile is the only way past the card. available(x) is (x.minLevel||1) <= G.level+1 && !G.upg[x.id] -- the level being OFFERED, not the one just finished. TAKEN tiles are gone for the run; DECLINED tiles (G.offered) come back only once the fresh pool runs thin, which is the fix for a real bug: the old filter burned every tile it had ever offered, and five draws x three slots against nine tiles left the level-5 and level-6 cards drawing from an empty pool. startLab() clears G.upg, G.offered, G.offer and G.picks.

name: LONGER STAR
summary: Extends the hypernova from 16 beats (9.231s) to 24 beats (13.846s); the tile prints 'about 14 seconds'.
detail: Tile id `longstar`, colour #ff4fd8. Read once, at the hypernova pickup: G.hyperD = SPB*(upgOn('longstar')?24:16). Nothing in tools/ ever sets it, so the effect is unasserted.

name: DEEP BANK
summary: Adds one to the starting shield bank -- 2 becomes 3 -- additively with the difficulty mode's own shields knob.
detail: Tile id `deepbank`, colour #7bffc8. G.shields = 2 + (upgOn('deepbank')?1:0) + MD().shields, so it literally means 'one more shield' in either mode. Unasserted by any harness.

name: SLOW WORLD
summary: Extends slow-mo from 6 seconds to 9.
detail: Tile id `slowworld`, colour #b48bff. Asserted in smoke.mjs by taking the orb again with the flag set and reading G.slow === 9.

name: RICH NOVA
summary: Each converted red leaves two stars instead of one, and the second walks the same spacing search so a doubled wall is a longer necklace.
detail: Tile id `richnova`, colour #ffffff. Read inside novaConvert, so it also doubles the yield of hypernova, mirror, scorch and slipstream conversions -- not just the nova's. Unasserted by any harness.

name: EARLY STARFALL
summary: Drops Starfall from three star-fed orbits to two; the id says nothing about what it does.
detail: Tile id `hairtrig` (docs/design/teaching.md still calls it HAIR TRIGGER). dropNeed() returns 2 with it and 3 without. dropcheck asserts both values.

name: LONG MAGNET
summary: Extends the Magnet field from 10 seconds to 16; the id is the retired Spotlight's, kept so saved G.upg keys survive.
detail: Tile id `stagelight`, colour #b48bff. Asserted in smoke.mjs: take the orb with the flag set and read G.spot === 16.

name: LONG MIRROR
summary: Extends the mirror from 16 beats (9.231s) to 24 beats (13.846s); the tile prints 'about 14 seconds'.
detail: Tile id `longmirror`, colour #4d8cff. Read once, at the mirror pickup. Unasserted by any harness.

name: DEEP BURN
summary: Extends scorch's active paint time from 8 seconds to 13; the wake's own per-sector lifetime is unchanged.
detail: Tile id `deepburn`, colour #ff8a2b. It lengthens how long new wake is laid, not how long a laid sector burns -- that stays max(2.6, one orbit at the current speed). Unasserted by any harness.

name: STEADY HAND
summary: Widens the tight-tap timing window from 0.032s to 0.045s -- the only tile that touches an input rather than a reward.
detail: Tile id `steadyhand`, colour #ffc857. Read in judgeTiming as W = upgOn('steadyhand')?0.045:TIGHT, where TIGHT is 0.032. Unasserted by any harness, and it is the tile whose inversion would be hardest to notice.

name: LONG SLIPSTREAM
summary: Extends slipstream from 12 seconds to 18; carries minLevel 2 so it is never offered before the orb exists.
detail: Tile id `longslip`, colour #5df0ff, minLevel 2 -- one of only two tiles with a floor. It first appears on the level-2 card. Asserted in smoke.mjs: G.slip === 18.

name: LONG STAR TRAIL
summary: Extends a star-trail route's life from 16 seconds to 24; carries minLevel 3 so it is never offered before the orb exists.
detail: Tile id `longtrail`, colour #ffc857, minLevel 3. Read in layStarTrail, so it applies to the route laid at pickup rather than to the orb's state. Asserted in smoke.mjs: every new route star carries life 24.

name: Two tile ids do not say what they do
summary: `hairtrig` is EARLY STARFALL and `stagelight` is LONG MAGNET; both ids were kept so saved G.upg keys survive their tiles being renamed.
detail: docs/design/teaching.md's wiring table still names HAIR TRIGGER and STAGE LIGHT; the shipped tiles print EARLY STARFALL and LONG MAGNET. Ids are unchanged, so check.mjs's wiring guard still passes and MECHANICS.md carries the current names. Grepping a display name finds nothing -- this is the same trap as warp/spot/hyper on the orb side.

name: Only five of eleven tiles have their effect asserted
summary: check.mjs proves every tile id has a live upgOn() call site; only slowworld, stagelight, longslip, longtrail and hairtrig are proved to change anything.
detail: The wiring guard matches against a comment-stripped copy of the source and has been blind twice: an id-after-name row was invisible to the old regex, and a call site surviving only inside a block comment satisfied the old test. It cannot tell a correct effect from an inverted one. Unasserted: longstar, deepbank, richnova, longmirror, deepburn and steadyhand -- which includes both duration tiles for the two newest orbs and the only tile that touches an input.

name: LONG FUSE (removed)
summary: The bass bomb's duration tile, cut with the orb it upgraded; it had been widening a clear region that was never drawn.
detail: Its removal left seven tiles; LONG MIRROR and DEEP BURN later brought that to nine, and LONG SLIPSTREAM and LONG STAR TRAIL to eleven. The lesson worth keeping is the one the review stated: an upgrade to an effect the player cannot see is an upgrade to nothing, and the tile made that visible before the orb's own illegibility was diagnosed.
